title: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.02875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In this paper, we consider mixed-motive games (MMGs) which model various real-world multi-agent scenarios where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. We identify an issue with existing gifting methods, where agents become overly dependent on incoming gifts and fail to learn reward-yielding behaviors, a phenomenon we call gift over-reliance. To address this, we propose a refusal-augmented gifting framework that balances cooperation and competition in MMGs. Our approach introduces an adaptive refusal mechanism that allows agents to selectively reject a portion of received gifts from their policy-update signals, thereby mitigating gift over-reliance and preventing the agents from being exploited by other agents. This mechanism is gifting-method-agnostic, serving as a plug-in for existing schemes while enabling decentralized learning. translated_title: AGiR：缓解混合动机博弈中的礼物过度依赖问题
translated_abstract: 本文研究混合动机博弈（MMGs），这类博弈模拟了各种真实世界的多智能体场景，其中自利智能体既需要合作又需要竞争。我们发现了现有送礼方法中的一个缺陷：智能体会过度依赖收到的礼物，无法学习产生奖励的行为，我们将这一现象称为“礼物过度依赖”（gift over-reliance）。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种拒绝增强的送礼框架，以在混合动机博弈中平衡合作与竞争。我们的方法引入了一种自适应拒绝机制，允许智能体选择性地将收到的部分礼物从其策略更新信号中剔除，从而缓解礼物过度依赖问题，并防止智能体被其他智能体利用。该机制与具体的送礼方法无关，可作为现有方案的即插即用插件，同时支持去中心化学习。我们证明，在多样的混合动机博弈环境和送礼方案中，我们的机制……
tldr: 提出了一种与送礼方法无关的自适应礼物拒绝机制AGiR，通过让智能体选择性地拒绝部分收到的礼物作为策略更新信号，缓解混合动机博弈中的礼物过度依赖问题，可作为即插即用模块兼容现有送礼方案并支持去中心化学习。
en_tdlr: AGiR introduces a gifting-method-agnostic adaptive refusal mechanism that allows agents to selectively reject a portion of received gifts from their policy-update signals, mitigating gift over-reliance in mixed-motive games while serving as a plug-in for existing gifting schemes and enabling decentralized learning.
